name: MultiMeter
description: Read an OWON B41T+ Bluetooth digital multimeter live inside Minerva. Your AI agent can read the current measurement, watch trends, press the meter's buttons, and record readings to CSV; the panel shows the live value with a rolling graph. Needs the meter powered on with its Bluetooth enabled and a Bluetooth radio on this computer; nothing else to install.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_status
tools.description: Meter connection state, identity, latest reading, recording state.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_read
tools.description: Latest measurement, optionally with recent history.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_press
tools.description: Press a front-panel button (select, range, hold, rel, hz, maxmin).

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_guide_set
tools.description: Show the user the target dial slot, lead jacks and an instruction in the guide panel.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_wait_for
tools.description: Block up to 25 s until the meter reports the wanted dial slot (and optionally a non-zero reading); with a cursor, answer at once if it already happened.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_changes
tools.description: What happened at the bench since a cursor: dial moves, settled values, probes lifted, OL, HOLD/REL, connect/disconnect. Call first after any pause.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_watch_start
tools.description: Arm a watch (dial reaches a slot, a non-zero reading settles, or any change) and end your turn; one line wakes your Minerva terminal when it happens or the timeout passes.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_watch_stop
tools.description: Disarm the watch before it fires.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_record_start
tools.description: Start logging readings to a CSV.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_record_stop
tools.description: Stop the recording and report the CSV path.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_record_export
tools.description: Copy the last recording to a chosen path (host save dialog when no path is given).

skills.title: Diagnose a circuit with the OWON B41T+ multimeter
skills.summary: Use when a person wants to measure or troubleshoot a circuit with the MultiMeter plugin: guide them step by step, prove each step from the meter itself, and show the meter face when a reading makes no sense.
skills.preconditions: The multimeter plugin is RUNNING (minerva_plugin_list; minerva_plugin_start id=multimeter) and minerva_multimeter_status reports connected. If not connected, tell the user to turn the meter on and enable its Bluetooth (the blue REL/Bluetooth button), then check again.
skills.outcome: The user has the measurement they came for, or a clear finding about what is wrong (no supply, open trace, wrong lead placement), each step confirmed by a reading from the meter rather than by asking.
skills.steps:
1. Ask what is under test and what value they expect (e.g. '3.3 V rail', 'is this fuse open').
2. Open the MultiMeter panel once: minerva_plugin_open_panel plugin_id=multimeter panel_name=multimeter_panel. It opens on the Meter view (a drawing of the meter face with a live reference card); setting a guide brings that view to the front, and the person can flip to the Data view (live value + graph) and back.
3. minerva_multimeter_guide_set with the slot (V for supply rails, OHM for continuity/fuses/resistors, mA/A/uA only for current), an instruction in their words ('black probe on ground, red probe on the 3.3 V pin'), and a warning when needed. Say the same thing in chat in one line.
4. minerva_multimeter_wait_for (timeout_s 25, re-call while the user is still moving) until matched. If it returns not matched, its live.slot tells you what the dial is actually on; say so ('the meter is still on ohms').
5. For a value: minerva_multimeter_wait_for nonzero=true once the probes are placed, then minerva_multimeter_read. Interpret against the expectation. Prefer minerva_multimeter_press select to switch DC/AC or ohms/continuity/diode rather than asking the user to touch the meter.
6. Reading is a hard zero on the right slot when a value was expected: do NOT guess. Point at the Meter view and ask 'is this how your leads are plugged in?' (red in VΩ for volts/ohms, black in COM), then whether the probes are on bare metal. Repeat step 5.
7. Current measurements: the meter cannot see which jack the red lead is in. Before the user probes, require an explicit 'moved it' for the red lead to the mA/uA or 20A jack, and remind them current is measured in series. Never let them put current-mode leads across a supply.
8. When done: minerva_multimeter_guide_clear, and offer minerva_multimeter_record_start if they want a trend.
skills.system_prompt: After any pause (the user kept working while you were not answering), call minerva_multimeter_changes first with the cursor from your previous call, and keep the new cursor; pass it to minerva_multimeter_wait_for so a step the user already finished counts. The meter reports its own dial position and value 2-3 times a second; use that instead of asking 'did you do it'. Slots: V, mV, OHM (ohms, continuity, diode via Select), HZ, CAP, TEMP, uA, mA, A. Red lead: VΩ jack for V/mV/OHM/HZ/CAP; mA µA TEMP jack for uA/mA/TEMP; 20A jack for A. Black lead always COM. Lead placement is invisible to the meter: the guide picture and the user's confirmation are the only checks. Keep each instruction to one physical action.

events.name: multimeter.reading
events.description: One decoded measurement, emitted for every packet the meter sends (2-3 per second).

events.name: multimeter.dial_changed
events.description: The dial moved to a new slot (or the first reading after connecting named it): one change-journal edge with kind dial.

events.name: multimeter.reading_settled
events.description: A reading held steady about a second at a value that differs from the last settled one: one change-journal edge with kind settled.
